usage: Use 訂造 when something is made specially to your own size, style, or design. It is common for clothes, jewellery, furniture, and other customer-made items.
It often works like an adjective before a noun, for example in phrases such as 訂造款 or 訂造戒指. In speech, people also say 訂造一個... or 去訂造...
This word is neutral and very common in everyday shopping talk. It sounds natural in shops, markets, and service situations where you want a custom fit or special order.
Learners should remember that 訂造 focuses on the act of making something to order, not just buying a ready-made item. It is close to 'custom-made' or 'made to order' in English.
